waivers.reason: The UI regression test executes Node with a fixed argv list and an in-memory scenario assembled only from the repository JavaScript helper. It never enables a shell or accepts user-controlled command arguments.
The test monkeypatches subprocess.run with a fake and merely constructs a CompletedProcess return value; no real process is spawned on this path.
Test double construction after monkeypatching subprocess.run; the stale-evidence runner under test never spawns a real process here.
Docker port probe stub returns a CompletedProcess object; subprocess.run itself is monkeypatched, so no process executes.
Docker run stub returns a CompletedProcess object; subprocess.run itself is monkeypatched, so no process executes.
Docker run stub returns a CompletedProcess object in the failure-cleanup test; subprocess.run itself is monkeypatched, so no process executes.
The bootstrap test invokes the current Python interpreter with a fixed Alembic argv prefix against an isolated tmp_path SQLite database; no shell is enabled.

The CLI contract test invokes the current Python interpreter with a fixed sync_rbac.py argv against an isolated tmp_path SQLite database; the command never comes from CLI input and no shell is enabled.

The e2e orchestrator's generic runner receives only argv lists assembled in the same script from fixed docker and pytest entrypoints; shell execution is disabled and failures surface as RuntimeError with captured detail.

The infrastructure verifier executes argv lists assembled by the same script from fixed docker and system tool entrypoints; output passes through the sensitive-value redaction filter and shell execution is disabled.
